summary: A class variable is shared by every object of the class. An instance variable belongs to one object. Use class variables for counters and values that are the same for everyone.
notes: Student.count += 1 updates the shared counter. self.count += 1 would create a separate count on that one object.
@staticmethod defines a method you call as Student.is_valid_id(1500) without any object.
leo.school = ... does not change Student.school. It adds a school field to leo only.
pitfall: Writing self.count += 1 in __init__ leaves Student.count at 0, because it creates an instance variable instead of changing the class variable.
